argument_summary: The current record does not support an unconditional clean certification. It does support a narrower position: operational launch readiness is evidenced by aggregate readiness clearing by 2.2 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 6% monitored rollout with rollback capability, while the same record also shows the disability accommodations intake segment remains exposed and below target, with no complete approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under that record, the supportable certification basis is conditional and limited: certification is defensible only as a monitored, reversible launch paired with explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the named limitation affecting the exposed use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim changes the policy analysis. The operational controls reduce deployment risk and make a bounded launch more defensible, which is relevant to whether escalation is necessary, but they do not convert the present record into clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the key constraint. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows neither predicate is satisfied here: the affected segment remains eligible for rollout, and the available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not cover that segment. The same policy also says disclosure is required unless the weakness is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, rollout controls support managed deployment but do not satisfy the policy predicate for treating the weakness as cured; they support, at most, a caveated certification position tied to explicit disclosure.
concessions: The present record does not establish that the required disclosure is already in place before launch.
The present record does not establish exclusion of the affected disability accommodations intake segment from the rollout cohort.
The present record does not establish approved risk acceptance covering continued exposure of that segment.
Any recommendation should be read as caveated certification, not as evidence that the documentation-sufficiency weakness has been resolved.
